Guidance & outlook: This is expected to grow by another 30% in the near future.
And earlier in the last earnings call, you had indicated that you are targeting 15% plus growth in this financial.
And also in Africa, we were targeting close to $120 million revenue in '27 versus $80 million that we did in '26.
Growth & demand: Our India business grew 16% year-on-year, supported in part by the transition to the lower tariff regime under Section 122, following the wind down of earlier IEEPA reciprocal tariff.
The significance of the growth is best understood in the context Indian apparel exports as a whole declined 12% year-on-year during the same period.

Turning to the demand environment. end consumer demand in both U.S. and U.K. recorded a strong growth through the first 6 months of CY '26, although the pace of growth in the U.S. has softened in June.
Margins & costs: Consolidated EBITDA rose 17% year-on-year, with India operations up 14%.
In Karnataka, the wage increase was 5%, which is really CPI linked, which is the annual DA increa se, which indexes the minimum wage to inflation.

One is the utilities cost, primarily the gas and fuel cost plus the chemicals cost, which has gone up substantially during this period., We have taken a hit close to around INR5 crores to INR6 crores during this period..
Capex & expansion: The unit has secured nominations from multiple brands for fabric sourcing, has started exporting fabrics as well and it's operating at a capacity of about 50 lakh meters a month.
Increasing capacity utilization, the investment in product mix and rising average realization will help in margin growth of BTPL.
We should be able to deliver the annual revenue with current capacity addition to about $120 million.
Balance sheet & cash: Against these pressures, we optimized overhead and grew on operating leverage to limit the financial impact.
We continue to look for ways to optimize our working capital with challenges like long shipping lead times notwithstanding.
We are selling FOB, but it still takes about 2 weeks to catch a ship and go, thereby us sitting on inventory and not able to realize our receivables until it is boarded into the ship.
Risks & challenges: This performance, while partly drawing from a weak Q1 of the previous year is an outcome of the sustained investment we have made in the region over several years.
So even though the rupee is much weaker than that, our 70% of our dollars were hedged, the rest 30% being covered by natural hedge through imports.
I think the -- some of the headwinds which we discussed are any possible changes to RoSCTL, any disruption to logistics, et cetera, U.S. retail demand and any tariff volatility.

Gokaldas Exports Limited May 25, 2026 Africa business declined by 19%, primarily impacted in the period up to Q3 due to AGOA uncertainties, leading to a reduced order book for that period, resulting in a revenue drop of about INR180 crores.
On demand front, U.S. and U.K. retail sales witnessed a strong growth of 8% and 6%, respectively, for CY '25.
Margins & costs: The capacity utilization at BTPL is approaching nearly 50 lakh meters per month, and the mill has currently a capacity of 70 lakh meters a month and can be raised to 100 lakh meters per month with an additional capital expenditure of about INR50 crores to INR60 crores.

So, if we look at it from that standpoint, and there's no externalities or external disruptions of a significant nature, then I think the India EBITDA margin should be of the order of 13%to 13.5%, whereas the Africa EBITDA margin should be about 10% to 10.5% for that year.
That's why despite their labor costs being high, and apparel is labor cost labor-intensive, they are offset with a lower cost of raw materials, fabric, even lower utility costs, etcetera, etcetera.
Capex & expansion: During the year, the company spent about INR170 crores towards new capacity creation, which will pay out in the years ahead.

Net debt has increased by INR395 crores, primarily driven by capex investments for incremental capacity expansion, additional investment s in BTPL and increased working capital on account of volume increase.
But to sustain our at least 15% kind of growth, we will definitely work on the capex that is required to manage that and to deliver that growth.
Balance sheet & cash: So, there is an overall increase of almost INR200 crores in working capital.
But at the current level of operation, our intention is to bring down our working capital to the extent of INR75 crores du ring this year from where we are at this point of time.
So should we expect the EBITDA from the year to go up by another 200 bps on an average because of the operating leverage.

Growth & demand: It grew by about 10% even as apparel exports from India declined, a clear gain in market share won by holding on to customers and executing dependably through tariff turbulence.

The Africa business declined 19% over the year, held back through the second and third quarters by uncertainty over the renewal of the African Growth and Opportunity Act; once that uncertainty cleared, it returned to healthy growth in the closing quarter.
The India business grew about 2%, and the Africa business recovered strongly in the fourth quarter, reporting 17% growth following the renewal of the African Growth and Opportunity Act.
Margins & costs: Sustained an EBITDA margin of 12.4% in India operations, supported by disciplined cost management alongside continued investment in long-term manufacturing capability.

Adjusted for the estimated ₹97 crore impact of United States tariffs and certain one-time costs, EBITDA stood at ₹530 crore at a margin of 13.0%, an improvement of 166 basis points that reflects the underlying health of the operating business.

The year carried an estimated one-time cost of around C97 crore arising from United States trade measures, compared with about C22 crore of one-off costs in the prior year; excluding this, EBITDA was C530.4 crore against C446.2 crore and the margin improved to 13.0% from 11.4%.
Capex & expansion: Growth-ready infrastructure: Advanced planning for the next phase of expansion, with FY27 capital expenditure guided at approximately ₹125 crore, towards modernisation and capacity expansion as recent additions are absorbed.

Net debt rose to C552.6 crore as on 31 March 2026 from C158.2 crore a year earlier, driven primarily by capital expenditure for incremental capacity, additional investment in the BTPL and higher working capital accompanying volume growth; total borrowings stood at C977.6 crore against C643.3 crore.
Net debt increased to ` 553 crores during the year, primarily due to capital expenditure on incremental capacity expansion, higher working capital requirements, and additional investments in BTPL.
Balance sheet & cash: Profit before tax fell 21% to ₹172 crore and profit after tax fell 37% to ₹100 crore, weighed down by the tariff impact, operating de-leverage in our Africa business, the start-up costs of newer initiatives, and higher finance and depreciation charges tied to our recent investments.

By geography, the India operations recorded an EBITDA margin of 12.4% and the Africa operations 2.3%, the latter reflecting operating de-leverage during the AGOA-related disruption in the middle of the year and the start-up costs of new initiatives.
Of the net debt, C87.6 crore was attributable to the India operations and C465.0 crore to the Africa operations.
Risks & challenges: Despite the tariff-related challenges, U.S. retail sales recorded healthy growth of 8% year-on-year (YoY) in 2025, while imports remained subdued, declining by 2% YoY during the same period.
